definition: A statistical framework for updating a belief (e.g. a prediction of prompt difficulty, or of how useful a training example will be) from prior assumptions plus observed evidence. In the archived sources it appears as the tool behind two training-efficiency methods: predicting which RL training prompts are informative from partial reward history, and a small, prompt-generic Bayesian predictor of prompt difficulty learned from shared optimization history, used to select prompts for efficient RL post-training of reasoning models.

evidence.note: Selects which training prompts to use for RL finetuning of large reasoning models by predicting their learning dynamics with a hidden Markov model, instead of evaluating every candidate with rollouts.
evidence.title: Dynamics-Predictive Sampling for Active RL Finetuning of Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Trains a small, prompt-generic Bayesian predictor of prompt difficulty from shared RL optimization history to select informative training prompts and reduce rollout cost when RL-training large reasoning models.
evidence.title: Small Generalizable Prompt Predictive Models Can Steer Efficient RL Post-Training of Large Reasoning Models

name: Bayesian inference
